# Review — iliad-079 (Iliad 13.169–265)

Reviewer, pass 1 (units.json). `t` untouched in every unit (checked: the units' `t` joined, word for word, equals the edition's lines 169–265 as the packet prints them, 682 words; every `ln` is the line on which the unit's first word stands; `p` is on exactly the seven paragraph starts 169, 206, 221, 231, 239, 254, 259; speech marks balanced, six speeches: “ on 219, 222, 232, 249, 255, 260 and ” on 220, 230, 238, 252, 257, 265, `mark` on all six opening units; the previous part ends at 168 outside any speech, and the speech opened at 260 closes at 265, the end of this part). No scansion flags in the packet; the two lines the scanner marks only as "spondaic fifth" (175, 232) were scanned by hand and are regular, so no sentence was added to any note.

Severity: high = wrong sense, wrong claim a reader would carry away, or a breach of a fixed house formula/epithet/stock phrase; medium = false grammatical label or false position claim, a single-word table conformity slip, or a misleading note; low = cosmetic or a loose statement.

### Cross-references checked

11.500 (βοὴ δ’ ἄσβεστος ὀρώρει, true after the fix); 164 and 167 of the last part (ἐχάζετο at 164, οἰσόμενος and λέλειπτο at 167, all true in iliad-078); 12.247 (μενεδήϊος, true); 2.450 (λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν, true); 13.119 (λυγρὸς ἐών, true); 4.448 (ὀμφαλόεσσαι, true); the notes' own references “as at 183”, “as at 210”, “as in 219”, “the same formula as at 221”, “(see 192)”, “the dual Αἴαντε of the last unit”, “the question at 250”, “as 240 and 247 show” are all true of the lines; the “201” at 190 was false and is fixed. The repeated lines were compared with the published English: 187 (fixed), 208 (identical to iliad-048), 221 and 259 (identical to iliad-023), 227 (identical to iliad-072's last line), 231 (identical to odyssey-063).

### Findings considered and refused

- **Drafter's flag, συμφερτὴ ἀρετή (237) “is a joint thing”.** Strange English, but the Greek says only that excellence is joint; “strength in numbers”, “worth pooled” and “valour” each decide more than the Greek says, and the note already states what is understood. Left (only “wretched” changed).
- **κρείων ἐνοσίχθων “lord earth-shaker”.** Right per the table; only the missing “the” in `l` was wrong.
- **“swift in feet” (249).** Matches the table's πόδας ὠκύς pair (“swift in feet” / “swift of foot”), ταχύς and ὠκύς both “swift”; the hyphenated form belongs to the epithet joined to a name. Left.
- **βουληφόρε.** `l` “counsel-bearer”, `i` “counsellor”, exactly the table's 5.180 pair; the note's claim is true. Left.
- **ὅ at 211.** The note gives the reading “who” (masculine, the wounded companion) and says some take ὅ as “because”; both are real, the sense is nearly the same, and `l`/`i` follow the first. Nothing false to correct. Left.
- **εἴσατο at 191.** From ἵεμαι “speed”, as the table has it (4.138, 5.538, 12.118); `l` “did it speed”, `i` “did not reach”; the note's disjunction with εἴδομαι is stated correctly. Left.
- **ἀκήριον (224).** The table (5.812) gives “spiritless fear”; the note correctly says the adjective could instead go with τινα, a real ambiguity (the adjective has one form for masculine and neuter). `l` keeps the English order “spiritless fear” where the table's `l` row follows the Greek order “fear … spiritless”; both are the same words, and a reordering in `l` would force a choice between the two readings. Left.
- **κατεάξαμεν (257).** The plural for the singular is real: ἔχεσκον and βαλών in the same sentence are singular. `l` “we broke”, `i` “I have broken” with the note saying the Greek has “we”; the “have” gives the aorist its present force (the spear is now gone). Left.
- **Anacoluthon 197–200.** Ἴμβριον is resumed by τὸν at 201, so “left unfinished” is loose but the note says where it is picked up; `i` “As for Imbrius, … —” reproduces the hanging accusative honestly. Only the invented “And” in `l` was removed.
- **ἔτι νοστήσειεν (232), `i` “never again”.** “Again” could suggest an earlier homecoming; `l` has the literal “not any more”, and “never again” is a normal rendering of ἔτι with a negative wish. Left.
- **κόμισαν (195).** `l` “carried”, `i` “carried off”: close; the table gives “carried off” for κομίζω (2.875), and the extra “off” in `i` is harmless. Left.
- **ἶσα τέκεσσι note (176).** The table has ἶσα φίλοισι τέκεσσι (5.71) with a different English (an idiom with “treating … as”); the note only says the same Greek phrase occurs there and the new-renderings row records `l`/`i` as following it. Not misleading. Left.
- **Ἕκτορι … ποδῶν (205).** `l` “before the feet of Hector” puts the dative into a genitive; the note says so and `i` “Hector’s feet” is the natural English. Left.
- **ὁρμηθέντος (183, 190) as “genitive absolute”.** True at 183 (no word to agree with); at 190 the note correctly says it agrees with Ἕκτορος. Left.
- **`i` “to see if we can be of some use, even though we are only two” (235–236).** “To see if” renders αἴ κε as the table does (2.72 “let us see if”); “only” is carried by καί … ἐόντε. Left.
- **“going to the war” vs `l` and ἔχε “have as wife” (173).** Both explained in the notes and recorded in `new-renderings.md`. Left.
- **Title “Idomeneus Arms”.** Can be misread as a noun phrase, but it is a verb phrase in the house style of the neighbouring titles and the part covers the arming; changing a title is outside this pass. Left.
- **Pass-1 reading of Greek → `l` → `i` word by word:** no further errors in case, tense, mood or particles beyond those above. Remembered-English check: no phrase in `i` that looked ready-made except the stock lines, which follow the table.

### Pass 2 — findings considered and refused

- **κατεάξαμεν “of a single speaker” (gloss).** A remark about use, but it is the whole reason the plural stands for the singular and is true of every occurrence in the poem’s speech; the entry is still general to the form. Left.
- **ἀκήριον entry (known).** The existing entry lists neuter nominative with δέος; the note’s alternative (with τινα) is only a possibility the text leaves open, not a different parse of the form’s role in this clause as the entry would have to carry. Left.
- **ἀφαρπάξαι, ἁρπάξαντε (gloss).** The infinitive could be read as an aorist optative in Aeolic spelling; no such reading is possible in this context. Left.
- **ἀγγελίης broadened entry.** The old entry says “message” and the new example “on some news”; the entries are glossary glosses, not the house renderings (which `l`/`i` follow). Left.
- **μάχεσθαι at 252.** Could be read as depending on a second λιλαίομαι understood; the entry’s “after λιλαίομαι” is true either way. Left.
- **Unit 190 note vs gloss ὁρμηθέντος.** Resolved in the gloss (above), not in the note, which was already right.
- **Titles, quotation marks, marks, paragraph marks, `ln`, cross-references.** Re-checked after the pass-1 edits: nothing broken. The pass-1 edits to `l`/`i` left no other stale word in a note (searched for brave, hurl, threw, message, leader, hostile, wretched, shout, drew, whirl, crowd, steadfast, bosses, stood out).
